links.comparator_used: Standard LLM generation without retrieval (few-shot and fine-tuned Qwen and BioBART)
links.outcome: Quality, factual consistency and readability of lay summaries
links.effect: RAG alone offered no benefit; the abstract gives no numbers. Combining RAG with NER degraded performance in few-shot settings but improved readability when fine-tuned.
links.tradeoff: Irrelevant retrieved terms can introduce hallucinations.
links.quote: Results show that NER consistently improves readability and overall quality, while RAG alone offers no benefit and can introduce hallucinations from irrelevant retrieved terms.

links.comparator_used: Standard LLM-based generation without NER-based entity extraction
links.outcome: Readability and overall quality of lay summaries
links.effect: NER consistently improved readability and overall quality; fine-tuned BioBART with NER achieved the best overall performance (no numbers in the abstract).
links.quote: Results show that NER consistently improves readability and overall quality, while RAG alone offers no benefit and can introduce hallucinations from irrelevant retrieved terms.

links.comparator_used: Few-shot prompting variants of the same models
links.outcome: Overall performance and readability of lay summaries
links.effect: Fine-tuned BioBART with NER achieved the best overall performance. Adding RAG to NER degraded few-shot results but improved readability when fine-tuned (no numbers in the abstract).
links.quote: Fine-tuned BioBART with NER achieves the best overall performance, highlighting entity-aware extraction as the primary driver of improved patient-friendly summaries.

design_hint: retrieval grounding and NER-based entity extraction added to LLM lay summarization
